statement_summary: Written program meets PCI DSS for service providers and the Safeguards Rule
Qualified Individual designated in writing and reaffirmed yearly
PCI DSS executive charter; responsible role per requirement per platform
Annual risk assessment and targeted risk analyses on every platform
Risk acceptance authority by level; no acceptance of a requirement not in place at the ROC
PCI DSS scope confirmed every six months and after significant change; organizational change review
Quarterly reviews that staff on every platform perform security tasks
Service provider due diligence, agreements, AOCs, responsibility matrices, annual Tier 1 review
AOC and responsibility matrix provided to merchants and ISVs on request
Annual written Qualified Individual report to the board audit committee; quarterly vCISO reports
Annual independent testing (internal audit and QSA); program adjusted after tests
Acquired environments on the SIEM, identity provider, PAM, and in scope within 90 days of closing
AI tools and models approved through the AI and model risk process
Unique identities; no shared accounts; sealed and tested break-glass accounts
Access by job need and least privilege from a role catalog
Workforce MFA; phishing-resistant MFA and PAM for administrators and CDE access
MFA for high-risk customer roles on every portal; approved dynamic analysis for others
All access including cloud keys and tokens removed by the end of the last day
Prior roles removed within 5 business days of a transfer
Six-month access reviews on every platform; quarterly reconciliation to HR
Service accounts scoped, vaulted, never hard-coded, reviewed every six months
No standing administrator roles; just-in-time elevation through PAM
Vendor remote access through PAM, approved per session, recorded
Step-up MFA, 3-business-day hold, and call-back for funding account changes
Cage access list reviewed quarterly; visitor escorts recorded
Written plan covering 314.4(h) and PCI DSS 12.10.1; card data and settlement runbooks
Security alerts on every platform monitored and answered 24x7
Severity 1 escalation to the COO within 1 hour; crisis management team; counsel-directed forensics
Card data compromise: evidence; sponsor bank within 24 hours; Visa within 3 calendar days; PFI
Four-hour covered services determination and notice to both banks; contacts confirmed quarterly
FTC notice decision within 30 days of discovery for 500 or more consumers
Card data found outside a CDE handled as a potential incident
Annual executive and technical exercises; settlement exercise with both banks every two years
Annual training for responders and crisis management team
Data classified and inventoried; reviewed with PCI DSS scope
Restricted data only in a CDE; tokens or masked PAN elsewhere
No sensitive authentication data after authorization, including call recordings
HSM-protected keys with dual control on every platform; DR replication after rotation
TLS 1.2 or higher or private encrypted links for external transmission
PAN retention limits (18 months in the archive); quarterly deletion process
Training data tokenized and minimized; PAN block on load; monthly scans
Monthly PAN discovery on non-CDE stores
Funding files released under dual control, validated, and signed
No card data in email, chat, tickets, or shared drives
Annual awareness training; annual secure coding for developers
Card data only through the secure payment flow with automatic recording pause
Approved AI tools only; no Restricted data; human review of outputs
AI-assisted code labeled and reviewed; security review for CDE repositories
